version.approval_notes: Third-party library: vendor/mux.min.js is mux.js 7.1.0 (Apache-2.0), unmodified official build — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mux.js@7.1.0/dist/mux.min.js (sha256 eb088a07f954554db7c38114487b21df6d1f28c4a84d53003644e962c7567b5b), source: https://github.com/videojs/mux.js/tree/v7.1.0. All other files are unminified source. The offscreen API reference in background.js is guarded by `chrome.offscreen` feature detection and is only used in the Chrome build; in Firefox the background page does the same work. The extension sends the video page URL to our server (videoner.download) only for platforms the browser can't download from directly (declared as websiteActivity). Cookies: the optional `cookies` permission and the optional `authenticationInfo` data collection permission are requested only when the user clicks "Connect account to the bot" in the toolbar popup (account-connect.js). The cookies of that one platform (e.g. instagram.com) are then sent over HTTPS to our server, which keeps only that platform's cookies, stores them encrypted and returns a one-time code; the user sends the code to our Telegram bot so it can download posts only that signed-in user can see (stories, private posts). The user can disconnect in the bot at any time; the popup also offers to revoke the permission. Nothing is sent without that explicit click. Privacy policy: https://videoner.download/privacy (section "Connected accounts"). To test downloads: open a YouTube video page and click the Download button in the bottom-right corner.
